second_order: turning the subreddit into QPR for April Fools
theme_note: These passages launch and inhabit the temporary QPR room through flairs, mock loyalty, club talk, songs, tributes, and policing pretend allegiance; what varies is whether members author the fiction, join it, or enforce it.
regrouped_from: Split from a preliminary all-QPR grouping after comparing exchanges: performing temporary allegiance differs from judging the makeover and from blaming it for the match loss.

second_order: questioning, judging, and asking to undo the QPR makeover
theme_note: These passages work out why the room changed, judge whether the joke is funny or overdue, ask for the Chelsea display back, and answer those objections; positions vary from confusion and rejection to defending the moderators' joke.
regrouped_from: Split from a preliminary all-QPR grouping because interpreting and contesting the makeover is a different practice from performing QPR allegiance.

second_order: talking through the match inside the QPR day
theme_note: These passages keep ordinary match watching, skill praise, relegation talk, player comparisons, and referee criticism going while the temporary QPR premise is recruited into parts of that talk; the amount of QPR play varies across passages.
regrouped_from: Split from the QPR-performance grouping because these passages primarily conduct match talk, even when the badge or adopted identity enters it.

second_order: blaming the QPR makeover and moderators for the loss
theme_note: These passages turn the football loss into mock or serious blame directed at QPR, the banner, the prank, and moderators, ranging from witchhunt jokes to demands, abuse, and calls for a moderator to leave.
regrouped_from: Split from general rejection of the makeover because these passages specifically make it or its moderators responsible for the loss.

second_order: accusing someone of vandalizing the green lattice
theme_note: This single passage makes an unexplained canvas-vandalism accusation; no other code establishes what the green lattice was or joins the same exchange.
regrouped_from: Reviewed against later damage reports and retained as a singleton because the passage never establishes that its green lattice is the Chelsea crest.

theme_note: This surviving title shares an r/place sighting without readable image content, a target, or a coordinating reply.
regrouped_from: Reviewed as a singleton because the record does not support grouping the unseen sighting with the later Chelsea crest project.

second_order: calling people together to put a Chelsea crest on r/place
theme_note: These passages recruit helpers, explain the canvas to newcomers, confirm that the effort is active, offer labour, and renew calls when participation is thin; what varies is whether the speaker initiates, answers, or amplifies recruitment.
regrouped_from: Merged recruitment across slices 05–07 after comparing what the exchanges do; separated from design decisions, pixel labour, and defence.

second_order: turning away from the crest attempt
theme_note: These passages decline the current Chelsea attempt, either by asking it to stop or by judging it late and redirecting effort elsewhere.
regrouped_from: Lifted from the recruitment grouping because refusing or redirecting the call is not the same practice as recruiting helpers.

second_order: working out the crest, coordinates, and what to finish
theme_note: These passages make or circulate templates, choose and change locations, identify landmarks, simplify the target, and negotiate what counts as a complete enough design; variation lies in location, scale, and reference-image disputes.
regrouped_from: Merged planning codes across successive crest threads; separated from actual placement and from off-platform coordination.

second_order: placing pixels, tracking progress, and keeping the build going
theme_note: These passages report first placements and completed letters, ask how long the work can last, maintain finished pixels, take shifts, and move from building to fixing; what varies is the stage of the build and the amount achieved.
regrouped_from: Merged progress and maintenance passages after following the build across slices 05–07; kept separate from recruitment and defensive repair.

second_order: moving crest decisions into private chat and bringing instructions back
theme_note: These passages move shared planning to ChelseaFC chat or Discord and return directions or reference images to Reddit; the unseen deliberation varies, but the movement of coordination is explicit.
regrouped_from: Split from general planning because venue movement and the return of instructions are the practice these passages share.

second_order: making room and deals with canvas neighbours
theme_note: These passages identify neighbours, revise an initial takeover complaint, trade borders and overlap, announce alliances, offer spare pixels, and ask nearby groups to coexist; relations vary from friction and boundary requests to reciprocal help.
regrouped_from: Merged neighbour-facing exchanges across the two main crest threads because each works out coexistence or reciprocal help; separated from defending against unattributed damage.

second_order: defending the crest and correcting friendly damage
theme_note: These passages label apparent sabotage, recruit defence, consider bots or scripts, repair stray pixels, protect intended red details, and discover that some damage came from misclicks or helpers following the wrong colour; variation is hostile, accidental, or ambiguous interference.
regrouped_from: Merged attack, defence, and correction passages after the later threads showed that apparent vandalism sometimes came from allies or defenders themselves.

second_order: thanking the builders and settling scores after place ended
theme_note: These passages celebrate survival, thank helpers and neighbours, allocate credit, recount overnight work and attacks, ridicule rivals, and interpret alterations to the finished crest; the retrospective varies between pride, qualification, retaliation, and indifference.
regrouped_from: Merged closing and retrospective codes from slices 07–08 because participants turn prior work into an achievement and rivalry account; kept separate from the labour as it happened.
